questions.title: Which beds are thirsty, and how much water do they need?
questions.why: SOSA gives each probe's reading and bed; AGROVOC names the crop, and the crop carries its threshold; the scene shows where to walk. Litres = shortfall x bed area x root depth.

questions.title: Where is powdery mildew likely, and which vent should open?
questions.why: Humidity is read per row (SOSA); susceptibility belongs to the crop concept (AGROVOC's powdery mildews, c_13557); the vents are in the scene. High humidity over a susceptible crop lights the beds and the vent above them.

questions.title: Which valves should open now?
questions.why: The valve-to-bed map is in the record; the valves are in the scene. Thirsty beds become a list of valves a grower can walk to, or an irrigation controller can be sent.

inference.title: All vegetable beds (and why basil is not one)
inference.why: AGROVOC is a SKOS thesaurus: tomatoes are fruit vegetables, which are vegetables; basil is a culinary herb, which is a plant product but not a vegetable. One rule over skos:broader answers a buyer's 'show me the vegetables' with the right beds.

fault_text: Bed B2's moisture probe is pushed into Bed B3, and Bed C2's valve was never entered in the irrigation record.
